deck.title: Similarities & Trends in the Properties of the Group 2 Metals, Magnesium to Barium, & Their Compounds

front_blocks.md: Why does the thermal stability of Group 2 carbonates and nitrates increase going down the group?

back_blocks.md: Going down the group, the metal cations become **larger** and have a **lower charge density**. This reduces their polarising effect on the carbonate or nitrate anion, so more heat is required to decompose the compound.

cards.front_md: Why does the thermal stability of Group 2 carbonates and nitrates increase going down the group?
cards.back_md: Going down the group, the metal cations become **larger** and have a **lower charge density**. This reduces their polarising effect on the carbonate or nitrate anion, so more heat is required to decompose the compound.

front_blocks.md: The solubility of Group 2 sulfates increases going down the group.

back_blocks.md: The solubility of Group 2 sulfates **decreases** going down the group. The enthalpy of solution becomes more endothermic because the lattice enthalpy decreases more slowly than the enthalpy of hydration.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The solubility of Group 2 sulfates increases going down the group.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The solubility of Group 2 sulfates **decreases** going down the group. The enthalpy of solution becomes more endothermic because the lattice enthalpy decreases more slowly than the enthalpy of hydration.

back_blocks.md: The **standard enthalpy of solution (Δ*****H***<sub>**sol**</sub><sup>**o**</sup>**)** is the energy absorbed or released when one mole of an ionic solid dissolves in sufficient water to form a dilute solution under standard conditions. It can be exothermic or endothermic.

cards.back_md: The **standard enthalpy of solution (Δ*****H***<sub>**sol**</sub><sup>**o**</sup>**)** is the energy absorbed or released when one mole of an ionic solid dissolves in sufficient water to form a dilute solution under standard conditions. It can be exothermic or endothermic.

front_blocks.md: What is the relationship between enthalpy of solution, enthalpy of hydration and lattice enthalpy?

back_blocks.md: The enthalpy of solution reflects the balance between the energy released on **hydration** of gaseous ions and the energy needed to overcome the **lattice**.

cards.front_md: What is the relationship between enthalpy of solution, enthalpy of hydration and lattice enthalpy?
cards.back_md:
Δ*H*<sub>sol</sub><sup>o</sup> = Δ*H*<sub>hyd</sub><sup>o</sup> − Δ*H*<sub>latt</sub><sup>o</sup>

The enthalpy of solution reflects the balance between the energy released on **hydration** of gaseous ions and the energy needed to overcome the **lattice**.

back_blocks.md: Going down Group 2, the charge density of the metal cation **decreases** and its polarising power on neighbouring anions **decreases**.

front_blocks.md: The solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases going down the group.

back_blocks.md: For hydroxides, the lattice enthalpy decreases faster than the enthalpy of hydration going down the group, making the enthalpy of solution more exothermic and the hydroxides more soluble.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases going down the group.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

For hydroxides, the lattice enthalpy decreases faster than the enthalpy of hydration going down the group, making the enthalpy of solution more exothermic and the hydroxides more soluble.

front_blocks.md: Explain why small Group 2 cations at the top of the group have a greater effect on polarising carbonate and nitrate ions than larger cations lower in the group.

back_blocks.md: Smaller cations have a **greater charge density** (same 2+ charge packed into a smaller volume). This produces a stronger electric field that distorts the electron cloud of the anion more, making the anion more polarised and easier to decompose thermally.

cards.front_md: Explain why small Group 2 cations at the top of the group have a greater effect on polarising carbonate and nitrate ions than larger cations lower in the group.
cards.back_md: Smaller cations have a **greater charge density** (same 2+ charge packed into a smaller volume). This produces a stronger electric field that distorts the electron cloud of the anion more, making the anion more polarised and easier to decompose thermally.

front_blocks.md: Why does the enthalpy of hydration of Group 2 cations become less exothermic going down the group?

back_blocks.md: Going down the group, the cations become **larger**. The ion-dipole interactions between the cation and water molecules weaken, so less energy is released when the gaseous ions are hydrated.

cards.back_md: Going down the group, the cations become **larger**. The ion-dipole interactions between the cation and water molecules weaken, so less energy is released when the gaseous ions are hydrated.

front_blocks.md: Barium sulfate is **..........**  in water, whereas barium hydroxide is **..........**  in water.

back_blocks.md: Barium sulfate is **insoluble** in water, whereas barium hydroxide is **soluble** in water.
